explanations: terra: No soul can discharge anything for another on Judgment Day, a boundary on the source dictionary sense of a sheep or charity sufficing on someone's behalf.
terra: The repeated warning again denies that one soul can suffice for another or that compensation can be accepted, reinforcing the eschatological limit on transferable discharge.
terra: God says He will complete His favor upon the believers so that they may be guided, joining the section's completed niʿma and hidaya in one promise.
terra: The Messenger recites, teaches, and purifies the community, supplying a non-financial use in which purification is mediated rather than self-claimed.
terra: One sign-complex contains rain from the sky, revived earth, dispersed animals, and governed clouds, bringing cloud, fertile ground, and herd under one divine ordering.

luna: This account of righteousness includes giving wealth, despite love for it, to kin, orphans, the needy, and travelers; it supplies recipients for the generous act at the center of the section. | terra: Birr includes giving loved wealth to vulnerable people alongside prayer and zakat, making costly transfer of māl a substantive sign of truthfulness and piety.

luna: This pilgrimage ruling calls for whatever offering is readily available when pilgrims are prevented, and requires it to reach its place; it gives the section's هدي a second concrete setting. | terra: The phrase فَمَا ٱسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ ٱلْهَدْىِ puts the source section's two dictionary branches together: y-s-r and the sacrificial animal called hady.

luna: The section's seed and tree images make giving productive; this ayah calls spending a good loan to Allah that He multiplies many times over. | terra: A good loan to God is multiplied many times, another direct formulation of giving that grows with God.
terra: Believers are told to spend from God's provision before a day when exchange and human alliances cannot operate, relating present giving to wealth's future inability to avail.

luna: The source section's root ز ك و is pictured as growth: a grain becomes seven ears in this account of spending, so giving returns more than the seed placed in the ground. | terra: Spending wealth in God's way is a seed growing seven ears with a hundred grains each, the Quran's explicit formulation of giving as crop multiplication.

luna: The section's giver seeks God's face rather than settling a human favor; this ayah says spenders who do not follow their gift with reminders or injury have their reward with their Lord. | terra: Spenders who do not follow gifts with reminders of favor or injury receive their reward with God, clarifying what it means to give without establishing a human debt.

luna: This ayah makes a kind word and forgiveness better than charity followed by injury, drawing a boundary around what counts as giving that benefits its recipient. | terra: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, specifying the relational boundary around the unencumbered gift in 2:262-264.
terra: A showy gift followed by reminders or injury is soil on bare rock: rain strips it clean, the precise failed-rain counterpart to the fruitful garden of 2:265.

luna: The source section links the giver to a fruiting palm; here a garden on high ground receives heavy rain and gives twice its produce, while its owner spends seeking Allah's pleasure. | terra: Spending to seek God's pleasure is pictured as a rain-fed upland garden that gives its crop twice over; this is the section's giver-tree, sought face, height, rain, and increase in one scene.
terra: A productive palm-and-grape garden is destroyed by a fiery whirlwind when its owner is most vulnerable, making the loss of accumulated yield a warning beside the multiplying garden of 2:265.

luna: The section ties giving to the growth of crops; this ayah commands spending from good things earned and from what the earth produces, while forbidding selection of inferior produce for charity. | terra: Believers must spend from their good earnings and from what God brings out of the earth, directly linking acceptable giving to agricultural produce.

luna: After the command to spend from good produce, this ayah sets Satan's threat of poverty against Allah's promise of bounty, a specific reversal of the fear that giving diminishes provision. | terra: Satan threatens poverty to deter spending while God promises forgiveness and bounty, exposing the two rival expectations behind withholding and giving.

luna: This ayah says public charity is good but secret charity given to the poor is better and expiates sins; it adds a private form of the face-seeking gift in the section. | terra: Concealed alms reach the poor and expiate wrongs, giving charitable transfer an explicit cleansing effect.

luna: The section's giver seeks Allah's face; this ayah explicitly says spending may be done seeking Allah's face and that whatever good is spent is repaid in full, relocating return from people to God. | terra: This ayah joins divine guidance to spending done only in seeking God's face and says the good spent returns to the giver, directly clarifying the motives and self-directed purification of 92:18-20.

luna: This ayah describes people spending wealth by night and day, privately and publicly, and promises reward without fear; it repeats the section's picture of giving wealth for God. | terra: Spending by night and day, secretly and openly, portrays constancy in giving and locates its reward with the Lord.

luna: The section explicitly distinguishes the root of ربا from the root of رَبّ; this ayah says Allah effaces ربا and causes charity to grow, setting false increase against blessed growth. | terra: God effaces usury and causes charities to grow, making the two opposed kinds of increase in the section an explicit divine contrast.
terra: Believers are commanded to leave outstanding usury if they are truthful, drawing the ethical boundary around the apparent financial growth rejected in 2:276.
terra: Only the principal may remain after usury is renounced, so neither party wrongs the other; this defines the non-growing amount against charitable multiplication.
terra: A debtor in hardship receives delay until ease, while waiving the debt as charity is better; financial ʿusr/yusr and voluntary release of what is owed meet in one ayah.

terra: A single inventory of worldly property includes gold and silver, marked horses, livestock, and cultivated fields, placing herd and crop together as the forms of māl that can captivate their owner.
terra: Mary's Lord causes her to grow a good growth and entrusts her to care, using plant increase for divinely nurtured human formation much as the section makes the giver a growing tree.

luna: The section's voluntary giver parts with wealth for Allah; this ayah says righteousness is not reached until one spends from what one loves, making the cost of giving explicit. | terra: People do not attain birr until they spend from what they love, paralleling 22:37's distinction between the material object offered and the inward quality that truly reaches God.
terra: The prohibition on consuming usury multiplied many times makes false financial increase visible as the opposite of the charity God multiplies.
terra: Spending in both ease and hardship shows that giving is not merely the overflow of abundance, a useful boundary for the source section's yusr imagery.
terra: The Messenger's recitation and instruction purify believers, clarifying another agent and means of the z-k-w process beside charitable purification.

luna: Those who withhold what Allah gave them from His bounty are warned that the withheld wealth will become a collar; this is a concrete reversal of the section's wealth given for purification. | terra: Those who withhold God's bounty wrongly think stinginess is good for them; what they withheld will encircle them, reversing wealth that purifies when released.

luna: This ayah condemns misers who urge others to be miserly and hide Allah's bounty, a social version of the section's withholding contrasted with the giver. | terra: The stingy command others to stinginess and conceal what God gave from His bounty, opposing both acknowledgment of niʿma and voluntary giving.

luna: Like the warning in 53:32, this ayah challenges people who claim to be pure and says Allah purifies whom He wills; it sets self-certification against God's judgment. | terra: Those who pronounce themselves pure are corrected: God purifies whom He wills, defining the divine boundary around the source section's self-purifying verb.
terra: Private counsel is justified when it orders charity or reconciliation, and action seeking God's pleasure is promised a great reward; motive again distinguishes the gift.

luna: The section defines هدي as livestock conveyed to the sanctuary; this ayah names the marked offerings sent to the Sacred House and describes pilgrims seeking bounty and approval from their Lord. | terra: The sacred state, sacrificial animals, and their garlands must not be violated, confirming هدي as a visible class of animals directed to the sanctuary.
terra: God declares His favor completed upon the community, a direct Quranic formulation of the dictionary sense cited for completing niʿma.
terra: The two sons offer sacrifices and acceptance is restricted to the God-fearing, a direct parallel to 22:37's insistence that the operative content of an offering is taqwa.
terra: Forgoing one's retaliation claim as charity becomes an expiation for the forgiver, a juridical example of voluntary giving that discharges a liability and cleanses.
terra: A hunting penalty must be هَدْيًا بَٰلِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ, an animal offering reaching the Kaaba, virtually the section's dictionary definition of hady brought to the sanctuary.

luna: The section's sanctuary offering is part of a wider rite: this ayah names the Sacred House, sacred month, and garlanded offerings as supports for people. | terra: The Kaaba, sacred month, sacrificial animals, and garlands are appointed as supports for people, again joining the sanctuary to hady livestock.

luna: Water brings forth vegetation, grain, clustered dates, and gardens of olives and pomegranates; this is a direct rain-to-harvest scene matching the section's cloud-grown plants and yielding palm. | terra: Rain produces every plant, grain, date clusters, grapes, olives, and pomegranates, and the reader is told to observe fruiting and ripening; it is a full scene of cloud-grown yield.

luna: This ayah describes people assigning shares of crops and livestock to Allah and their partners, then misallocating the shares; it provides a concrete contrast to the section's due crop and sanctuary offering. | terra: People divide crops and livestock between God and invented partners, a corrupt allocation that exposes why the harvest gift must be directed sincerely to God.
terra: Pagans assign what lies in livestock wombs exclusively to males and forbid it to females, a corrupt herd rule that combines the section's animals, sex distinction, and womb.

luna: The section's crop image reaches its due at harvest; this ayah commands giving the crop's حق on harvest day, joining field yield to an obligation of giving. | terra: The command to give the crop's due on harvest day turns agricultural yield into an obligation of giving, exactly the harvest-right scene developed in the section.

luna: This ayah divides livestock into burden-bearing and smaller kinds and permits eating from God's provision, concretizing the herd's labor and wealth. | terra: Livestock include burden-bearers and smaller animals, and people may eat God's provision; this adds a Quranic classification of the herd as useful rizq.

luna: The sheep and goats are presented as male-female pairs; this connects the section's agricultural dictionary senses of masculine and feminine to a Quranic distinction within herds. | terra: Pairs of sheep and goats are questioned by male, female, and what the females' wombs contain, a literal herd counterpart to the section's male/female and reproductive imagery.

luna: The same male-female question is applied to camels and cattle, extending the section's sexed herd image to its named desert wealth. | terra: Pairs of camels and cattle are likewise tested against male, female, and womb contents, placing the section's desert animal and sex vocabulary in the same scene.
terra: Prayer and sacrifice, together with life and death, are declared wholly for God, Lord of the worlds, stating the exclusive orientation of the animal offering.

luna: This ayah sends rain-laden clouds toward dead land and brings forth fruit; 7:58 supplies the land's distinct response, while this row contributes the cloud and rain that grow it. | terra: Winds carry heavy clouds to dead land and rain produces every fruit; it supplies the cloud action whose differing results are judged in 7:58.

luna: The source section names fertile, plant-ready ground and coarse growth; this ayah contrasts good land whose plants emerge by its Lord's permission with bad land that yields little. | terra: Good land brings out vegetation by its Lord's permission while bad land yields only meagerly, a direct boundary between fit soil and coarse or unfruitful growth.
luna: This ayah says belief and taqwa would open blessings from heaven and earth, but denial brings seizure; it joins the section's fearful giver and denier to the reversal of provision.
terra: Whatever believers spend in preparation is fully repaid without injustice, a specific promise of return that contrasts with giving in order to collect a human favor.

luna: The section's man gives his wealth for purification; this ayah condemns religious leaders who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way, the contrary use of property. | terra: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God's way embody the withholding opposite to the section's giver.

luna: The hoarded wealth in the preceding warning is heated and used to brand its owners; this gives bodily force to the section's claim that property cannot rescue its possessor. | terra: The hoarded metal is heated and brands their bodies, turning retained wealth into the punishment from which charitable purification would have separated them.
terra: People criticize the allocation of charities and are content only when they receive a share, revealing a self-interested stance around the same collection system named in 9:60.
terra: Those involved in charity distribution are told to be content with what God and His Messenger give and to desire God, the receptive counterpart to giving without bargaining.

luna: The section identifies the ساعي as one appointed to collect charity; this ayah names العاملين عليها among the recipients, placing administrators within the alms system. | terra: The recipients of alms explicitly include وَٱلْعَامِلِينَ عَلَيْهَا, the officials who collect them, corresponding to the dictionary sense of sāʿī as zakat collector.
terra: Some promise that if God gives them bounty they will give charity and become righteous, setting up an explicit test of whether received increase will be shared.
terra: When bounty comes they are stingy and turn away, reversing the truthful giver and making the failed promise resemble the section's kadhaba branch.

terra: The mockers target both voluntary almsgivers and those who find only their own effort to give; the latter embody the section's giver who comes by his own striving instead of waiting for collection.
terra: Those unable to find means for an expedition leave in tears because they have nothing to spend, a specific picture of voluntary expenditure constrained by lack of property.
terra: Some desert Arabs treat expenditure as a punitive liability and await misfortune, the exact motivational opposite of 9:99 and of giving for God's face.
terra: Some desert Arabs treat expenditure as nearness to God and a means to the Messenger's prayers, embodying the sincere alternative to payment regarded as a levy.

luna: The source section's root ز ك و appears in the command to take charity from people's wealth to purify them and make them grow; here the Prophet is the collector the commentary sets beside the self-initiated giver. | terra: The Prophet is told to take charity from their wealth so that it cleanses and causes them to grow, staging both the collector and the purifying growth of the giver.

luna: Following 9:103, this ayah says Allah accepts repentance and takes charities; 9:103 contributes the Prophet's taking and purification, while this neighbor identifies the ultimate receiver. | terra: God is the one who accepts repentance and takes charities from His servants, completing the collection scene while shifting its ultimate receiver beyond the human collector.

luna: Rain-fed plants flourish and then are cut down as if they had never grown; the ayah contrasts expected harvest with the sudden limit of possession. | terra: Rain-swollen vegetation is suddenly reaped as though it had not flourished the day before, a field-scale parallel to milk mistakenly expected to continue.
luna: Noah calls his people to seek forgiveness, then promises rain from heaven and increased strength; it directly joins repentance to renewed provision and growth.
luna: The king's dream places fat cows beside lean cows and green ears beside dry ones; it makes livestock and field produce images of abundance and scarcity together.
luna: Joseph advises sowing for seven years and leaving most grain in its ears; this is a concrete way of preserving crop abundance across lean years.
luna: The following years consume what was stored, except a little; this reverses the section's growing flock and fruiting field into provision running short.
luna: A year of abundant rain and pressing follows the famine, completing the cycle from scarcity back to plentiful yield.
terra: During famine, Joseph's brothers bring scant merchandise, ask for full measure, and request charity; agricultural scarcity, measured provision, and the giving sense of ṣ-d-q meet.
terra: The earth contains every kind of fruit in pairs, reinforcing the movement from male and female creation to paired fertility in the field.

luna: The section distinguishes plant-suitable soil from coarse ground; this ayah contrasts neighboring gardens and crops watered with the same water but producing different fruits. | terra: Adjoining soils, vineyards, crops, and palms receive one water yet yield differently, a close Quranic elaboration of fit earth and unequal fruitfulness.
terra: Those who remain patient seeking the face of their Lord also spend from God's provision secretly and openly, an exceptionally close meeting of the motive and act in 92:18-20.
terra: God promises increase in response to gratitude, making the true enlargement of blessing a relation to its divine giver.

luna: A good word is likened to a good tree with firm roots and branches reaching high; this extends the section's giver-as-fruiting-tree image. | terra: A good word is a good tree with firm roots and branches in heaven; with 14:25 it supplies the full image for the giver who grows as a fruit-bearing tree.

luna: The tree gives its fruit at every season by its Lord's permission, a close parallel to the section's person who grows by giving. | terra: The good tree تُؤْتِىٓ أُكُلَهَا every season by its Lord's permission, joining the section's itāʾ as fruiting, growth, and dependence on Rabb.

luna: The bad word is likened to a bad tree pulled from the ground without stability, the reversal of the fruiting, rooted tree image. | terra: A corrupt word is an uprooted tree with no stability, the barren inverse of the fruitful tree that gives by its Lord's permission.
terra: Prayer and secret or open spending are commanded before a day without trade or friendship, another specific boundary between transferable wealth now and useless wealth later.
terra: Fertilizing winds are sent and water descends for people to drink, offering a natural counterpart to the section's gendered fertility and cloud-grown field.

luna: This ayah names livestock as warmth and benefits for people; it gives concrete grounds for the section's claim that desert herds are wealth. | terra: God creates livestock with warmth, benefits, and food for people; this establishes why anʿām can be the desert's māl and niʿma.

luna: The section quotes the flock's beauty at evening return and morning release; this ayah is that precise herd scene. | terra: The herd has جمال when driven home and sent out to pasture, supplying the section's named daily scene of desert wealth.

luna: This ayah describes livestock carrying loads to distant places people could not reach without hardship, another material use of the herd that the section calls property. | terra: Livestock carry heavy loads to distant places people could scarcely reach themselves, extending the concrete value of the desert herd named in 16:5-6.
terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are provided for riding and adornment, extending 16:6's beauty-at-the-herd scene to the other animals of desert property.

luna: Rain sent down from the sky grows plants from which people pasture animals; this directly joins the section's cloud-grown field to its herds. | terra: Water descends from the sky for drink and produces the vegetation in which livestock graze, joining cloud, pasture, and herd in a single causal scene.

luna: The rain's yield includes olives, date palms, grapes, and other fruits; this supplies the very fruiting trees and crops behind the section's growth image. | terra: The same water grows crops, olives, palms, grapes, and every fruit, supplying the plant increase and date yield behind the section's paired verbs of giving and growing.
terra: Every blessing people possess is from God, clarifying why the section's gift can bypass human repayment and seek the Lord alone.
luna: This ayah says water from the sky revives the earth after its death, making rain the hinge between cloud and growing land.

luna: This ayah explains milk as a pure drink produced within cattle; it gives the section's changing milk supply its bodily source. | terra: Livestock contain pure, palatable milk drawn from within their bodies, supplying the concrete household substance behind the section's secondary senses of yusr and kadhaba as milk increasing or failing.

luna: The fruits of date palms and grapevines become provision; this extends the section's date-palm yield image to a Quranic account of fruit and drink. | terra: Date and grape fruits yield both intoxicant and good provision immediately after the livestock-milk ayah, placing animal drink beside the productive fruit tree.

luna: This ayah says those favored with more provision do not return it to those under their authority so they become equal; its own contribution is withheld surplus, while 16:72 continues with spouses, offspring, good provision, and denial of favor.
luna: This ayah joins spouses, children, grandchildren, and good provision, echoing the section's links between fertile herds, offspring, and material wealth.
terra: Tents from livestock hides and furnishings from wool, fur, and hair depict exactly how the herd constitutes the portable wealth of desert life.
terra: Immediately after the livestock-hide dwellings of 16:80, God says He thus completes His favor upon people, matching the section's dictionary claim that Rabb completes niʿma.
terra: What people possess runs out while what is with God remains, supporting the section's transfer of wealth toward the enduring divine face.
luna: A town once secure and supplied from every direction denies Allah's favors and is made to taste hunger and fear; it reverses the section's fruitful herd and crop into scarcity after denial.
terra: The one who seeks the hereafter, strives for it properly, and believes has his striving thanked; sought end and personal effort are explicitly joined.

luna: The source section explains ر ب ب through gradual upbringing; this prayer uses رَبَّيَانِي for parents who raised the speaker, a remembered human favor unlike the section's donor who owes no repayment.

luna: The command to give relatives, the poor, and the traveler their due uses the source section's root ء ت ي in a direct distribution of wealth, then forbids waste. | terra: The relative, needy person, and traveler must be given their due, another direct formulation of a right contained within one's provision.
luna: This ayah says that if people owned the treasuries of their Lord's mercy they would still withhold for fear of spending; it sharpens the section's contrast between generosity and miserliness.
terra: Two grape gardens ringed by palms and crops begin a parable in which abundant yield becomes the setting for false confidence in wealth.
terra: Both gardens give their full produce without withholding anything, a concrete Quranic use of آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا for the fruit-bearing sense attached to يُؤْتِى in the source section.
terra: The owner boasts that he exceeds his companion in wealth and people, joining agricultural fruit to the māl whose imagined sufficiency the section denies.
terra: He enters his garden wronging himself and says it will never perish, echoing the expectation of continued yield behind the section's prematurely failing milk.
terra: His companion says he should have acknowledged God's will and power on entering the garden, locating increase under the Lord rather than the owner.
terra: The companion expects his Lord may give him a better garden and send a calamity upon the boaster's, setting divine gift against possessed yield.
terra: The garden's water may sink beyond recovery, specifying how its continuing growth can be cut off.
terra: The fruit is destroyed and its owner wrings his hands over what he spent while the trellises lie fallen, making wealth and crop fail together.
terra: No group can help the owner apart from God and he cannot help himself, corresponding to wealth that cannot avail when its owner falls.
terra: The episode ends by locating true protection and the best outcome with God, restoring the Lord as the source and end of increase.

luna: Worldly life is likened to rain-fed vegetation that becomes dry fragments; this gives the section's growth-and-wealth image a specific account of transience. | terra: Worldly life is vegetation mingled by rain and then scattered dry by winds, sharpening the difference between temporary increase and what remains with the Lord.

luna: This ayah calls wealth and children adornments of worldly life and lasting righteous deeds better; the section's giving turns wealth into an act with an enduring moral value. | terra: Wealth and children are the adornment of nearer life while enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord, distinguishing held property from the lasting Godward act.
terra: John receives tenderness and purity from God and is God-fearing, a compact meeting of z-k-w and taqwa as divine gift and human quality.
terra: Moses uses his staff to beat down leaves for his sheep, a remembered Quranic detail of the daily care by which the herd is sustained.

luna: This ayah says God brings out paired kinds of plants; it connects the section's gendered plant vocabulary to Quranic language of differentiated vegetation. | terra: God makes the earth serviceable, sends rain, and brings out diverse pairs of plants, uniting fit soil, cloud, paired vegetation, and divine nurture.
terra: People eat those plants and pasture their livestock in them, completing 20:53's rain-and-growth scene with the herd.
terra: David and Solomon judge a cultivated field damaged when a people's sheep stray into it by night, a literal meeting between the section's two economic images, herd and crop.
terra: God gives Solomon the right understanding of the sheep-and-field case, so the scene's competing property claims remain subject to divine judgment rather than mere ownership.

luna: Water makes the earth swell and produce every kind of beautiful growth; the ayah then compares human formation in the womb, joining soil and gestation. | terra: Embryonic stages in wombs and barren earth that stirs, swells, and grows every delightful pair after rain make human gestation and fertile soil interpret each other.

luna: The pilgrimage offering is food from livestock over which God's name is mentioned, with a command to feed the needy; this makes the section's herd and sanctuary gift a public act of provision. | terra: Pilgrims name God over the livestock He provided, then eat and feed the destitute; a provided herd is turned into voluntary worship and sustenance.
terra: Within the pilgrimage-sacrifice passage, livestock are declared lawful and false speech forbidden, placing the offered herd beside the truth/denial boundary.
terra: Honoring God's sacrificial signs is said to arise from the piety of hearts, preparing the precise claim in 22:37 that taqwa, rather than meat or blood, reaches God.
terra: Sacrificial animals provide temporary benefits and then reach their appointed place at the Ancient House, joining useful herd wealth to its sacred destination.

luna: Each community is given a rite in which God's name is mentioned over livestock He provided; it joins the section's sanctuary animal to provision from God. | terra: Every community receives a rite in which God's name is spoken over the livestock He provided, placing ritual direction, gift, and بهيمة الأنعام in one frame.
terra: In the sacrificial-animal passage, the humble fear when God is named, endure, pray, and spend from His provision; this supplies the piety and giving that 22:37 says reach God.

luna: The source section's هدي is an animal brought to the sanctuary; this ayah describes sacrificial camels, their marked status, and feeding from them, giving the offering a concrete ritual scene. | terra: The sacrificial camels are signs of God, contain good, are slaughtered in His name, and feed both the contented and the petitioner; the herd becomes worship and provision for others.

luna: The same offering scene says their meat and blood do not reach Allah but taqwa does, and commands magnifying Him for guidance; it joins the offered animal, piety, and هدى exactly as the section does. | terra: The sacrificial herd, guidance, and piety meet explicitly: neither flesh nor blood reaches God, but taqwa does, and the worshippers magnify Him for having guided them.
terra: Rain turns the earth green and is followed by divine gentleness and awareness, a concise scene of growth under God's care.
terra: Human creation begins from an extract of clay, opening a stepwise formation that links earth and embodied growth.
terra: The human is then placed as a drop in a secure resting place, supplying the womb setting recalled in the section.
terra: Successive transformations carry the embryo toward another creation, a Quranic enactment of nurture from state to state toward completion.

luna: Water is sent down in measure and made to remain in the earth; this gives the section's rain-fed growth an image of measured provision. | terra: Water descends from the sky in due measure and is lodged in the earth, while God can also remove it; the source of continuing yield is both fitted and revocable.

luna: From that water come gardens of date palms and grapes with abundant fruit; this is a direct field-and-tree counterpart to the section's growing produce. | terra: That measured water grows gardens of palms and grapes with abundant fruit, supplying the exact fruiting increase that the section attaches to itāʾ.
luna: A tree growing on Sinai yields oil and food; it makes the section's fruitful tree image concrete in another provision-bearing species.

luna: The section contrasts increasing and drying camel milk; this ayah calls livestock a sign, names the drink from their bellies, and notes their other benefits. | terra: Livestock are a lesson: God gives drink from their bellies and places many benefits and food in them, directly presenting herd, milk, provision, and benefit together.
terra: People are carried on livestock and ships, continuing 23:21's milk-and-benefit scene with transport.
terra: No one would ever become pure without God's grace and mercy; this guards the agricultural metaphor from making the giver the independent cause of his own growth.

luna: Pure water is sent from the sky; this gives the section's cloud-grown field a second direct rain scene. | terra: Winds announce mercy and pure water descends from the sky, providing the cloud-borne source of the section's plant nurture.

luna: The water revives dead land and is provided for people and livestock, explicitly joining crops to the herd. | terra: That water revives dead land and gives drink to abundant livestock and humans, directly joining pasture-making rain to the herd it sustains.
terra: The earth grows every noble pair, a compact parallel to the section's gendered language for productive soil and plants.

luna: The section says property will not help its owner at his fall; this ayah says neither wealth nor children benefit on the Day when people are raised. | terra: On the Day of Judgment neither wealth nor children benefit, directly repeating the boundary in 92:11 on what māl cannot do when its owner falls.
luna: After denying that wealth and children avail, this ayah names a sound heart as what matters; it clarifies the inward end beside the section's act of giving to purify.
terra: The people are told to fear the one who supplied everything they know, introducing a concrete inventory of livestock and gardens as divine provision.
terra: The provision is specified as livestock and sons, explicitly placing the herd among the favors supplied by God.
terra: Gardens and springs follow the livestock, completing the field-and-herd abundance for which the people owe recognition.
terra: God sends rain and grows splendid gardens whose trees humans could not grow, directly assigning the crop's nurture to the Lord.
terra: Qarun's immense treasures make wealth the visible basis of arrogance at the opening of a downfall scene.
terra: Qarun attributes his wealth to his own knowledge, the self-sufficient claim opposite to yield recognized as the Lord's nurture.
terra: The earth swallows Qarun and his house, and no group or self-help saves him, graphically enacting wealth's failure when its owner falls.
terra: Observers then acknowledge that God expands and restricts provision, relocating increase and decrease with the true provider.
terra: Everything perishes except God's face, making explicit why wealth may be released for the one object that remains.
luna: Asked who sends water from heaven and revives the earth after its death, people answer Allah; it makes the source of the section's field-growth explicit.

luna: This ayah commands giving relatives, the poor, and travelers their due while seeking Allah's face; it joins a material right to the motive the section assigns its giver. | terra: Giving relatives, the needy, and the traveler their due is declared best for those seeking God's face, matching both the harvest-right and face-seeking motives of the section.

luna: The section's root ز ك و names giving for purification, and this ayah names zakat given seeking Allah's face as multiplying; the same verse contrasts it with ربا, which does not grow with Allah. | terra: Money advanced to grow in people's wealth does not grow with God, whereas zakat given seeking His face is multiplied; this is the section's exact boundary between apparent and real increase.

luna: God sends winds that stir clouds, spreads them, and brings rain from them; this gives the section's plant-growing cloud its motion. | terra: God sends winds, spreads clouds, and releases rain as He wills, spelling out the cloud process presupposed by the section's rabāb image.
luna: People despair before the rain comes; the ayah adds the reversal from withheld water to received provision.

luna: The effect of God's mercy is seen in earth revived after death; the rain-grown field becomes a sign of divine giving. | terra: The effects of God's mercy are read in His revival of the earth after death, making crop growth a sign of the giver behind it.
terra: God spreads creatures through the earth and grows every noble pair after rain, again joining created pairs to cultivated increase.
terra: Neither parent nor child can avail the other before the Lord, making family relation itself unable to settle the final liability.

luna: Water is driven to barren land and crops grow for people and livestock to eat; this is a precise meeting of the section's rain-grown field and herds. | terra: Water is driven to barren land and brings out crops eaten by both livestock and people, closely matching the section's joined herd-and-field economy.
terra: Men and women who give charity are named in parallel among the faithful qualities God rewards, joining the section's male/female pair directly to almsgiving.
terra: When the people of Saba turn away, the flood replaces their two gardens with bitter, sparse growth, a large-scale reversal of blessed crop increase.
terra: The ruined yield is identified as recompense for ingratitude, connecting lost provision with failure to recognize the giver.
terra: The affluent claim that greater wealth and children secure them against punishment, another false inference from visible increase.
terra: Wealth and children do not bring anyone near to God; faith and good action do, distinguishing possessed abundance from the quality that reaches Him.

luna: The section says worldly wealth cannot save its owner at his fall; this ayah answers the fear of losing wealth by saying Allah replaces what is spent, from whom provision comes. | terra: Whatever people spend, God replaces it as the best provider, giving the section's non-transactional gift a divine rather than human return.
terra: Winds raise clouds that God drives to dead land and revives with rain, another full cloud-to-field enactment of nurture.

luna: The source section's root ز ك و is used here for one who purifies himself; the ayah says that purification benefits the person himself, clarifying where its gain returns. | terra: Whoever purifies himself does so for his own soul, directly explaining how the wealth-giver's act increases and cleanses its giver rather than enriching God.

luna: Those who recite, pray, and spend from God's provision are described as hoping for a trade that will never perish; this turns the section's gift into lasting return. | terra: Those who spend secretly and openly hope for a commerce that will never perish, reversing the apparent loss of wealth in giving.

luna: The next ayah promises full payment and an increase from God's bounty; 35:29 contributes the non-perishing trade, while this row contributes its promised return. | terra: God fully repays their rewards and increases them from His bounty, supplying divine increase and recompense for the sincere spender.

luna: Dead earth is a sign for people, and grain is brought out for them; this directly joins land's revival to food. | terra: A dead field is revived and grain is brought out for people to eat, presenting agricultural growth as a divine life-giving sign.

luna: Gardens of date palms and grapes are made in the revived land, echoing the section's yielding trees. | terra: Gardens of date palms and grapes with flowing springs supply the exact fruit-bearing landscape behind the section's itāʾ and zakā imagery.

luna: The fruits are food for people, while the ayah asks why they do not give thanks; it links yield to its source rather than human ownership. | terra: People eat the fruit although their hands did not create it, setting received provision against any self-sufficient claim to growth.

luna: This ayah names pairs among what the earth grows and in people; it relates the section's masculine and feminine plant vocabulary to paired creation. | terra: The Creator makes pairs in what the earth grows, in human beings, and beyond their knowledge, directly supporting the section's extension of male and female into cultivated ground.
luna: When told to spend from what Allah provided, the deniers ask whether they should feed those whom Allah could feed; this is a direct refusal of the section's voluntary giving.

luna: This ayah asks whether people see the livestock God made for them and placed in their possession, directly staging herd as property. | terra: Humans are made owners of livestock God created for them, closely matching the section's opening identification of the desert household's property with its herd.

luna: The livestock are made manageable for riding and eating; the ayah adds uses to the herd's beauty and milk in the section. | terra: The livestock are subdued for riding and eating, showing how herd wealth is made fit for its owner.

luna: The livestock bring benefits and drinks; this is another direct account of the herd as provision. | terra: The herd supplies benefits and drinks, completing the milk-and-wealth scene and calling for gratitude for the provision.
terra: Abraham's son is ransomed with a great sacrifice, a distinct sacrificial-animal scene in which an offering discharges what was otherwise due.
terra: A man with ninety-nine ewes demands his brother's sole ewe, a herd scene in which taking one animal is an unjust seizure rather than the rightful charitable due developed in the section.
terra: David identifies the demand for the lone ewe as wrongdoing and warns that partners often transgress, distinguishing compulsory injustice from a sheep voluntarily or lawfully given.

luna: This ayah names eight pairs of livestock and says people are formed in their mothers' wombs; it joins the section's paired sexes, herd, and hidden gestation. | terra: Human creation, eight livestock pairs, and formation in mothers' wombs are placed together under the one Lord, uniting the section's sexed earth, herd, womb, and gradual nurture.

luna: Water produces plants of varied colors, then they turn yellow and become debris; this gives the crop-growth image a clear limit in passing away. | terra: Rain becomes varied crops that flourish, yellow, and crumble, making the stages and ending of agricultural increase visible.
terra: The liar who rejects truth is set under judgment, supplying the negative k-dh-b side of the truth-confirming, God-fearing figure in 39:33.
terra: The one who brings truth and confirms it is identified with the God-fearing, joining ṣ-d-q and taqwa as the positive counterpart to denial.
terra: Dust, drop, clot, childhood, maturity, and old age form an extended sequence of divinely governed development toward completion.
terra: God appoints livestock for riding and eating, explicitly presenting the herd as a divinely fitted provision.
terra: Livestock yield benefits, carry people to needs in their breasts, and share the transport role of ships, expanding the practical content of herd wealth.

luna: Lifeless earth comes alive after rain; the ayah makes the field's revival a sign of the One who gives it life. | terra: Humbled earth stirs and swells when water descends, and its reviver is identified as the giver of life, assigning fertility beyond the soil itself.
terra: God makes pairs from humans and from livestock and multiplies creatures through them, joining male and female, herd, and increase in one formulation.
luna: Rain descends after people have despaired, and mercy spreads; this matches the section's cloud as a source of renewed growth.
luna: This ayah says God grants daughters or sons as He wills; it connects the section's fertility and offspring image to human generative provision.
luna: The same passage allows both sexes or barrenness, setting reproductive abundance beside its withholding as the section sets growing and drying milk.

luna: Water is sent down in measure and dead land is revived; this repeats the section's connection between measured provision and crop growth. | terra: Measured water revives a dead land, linking provision in due measure to the field's restored capacity to grow.
terra: The Creator of all pairs also provides ships and livestock for riding, joining paired creation and herd utility as the section does.
terra: Riders are told to remember their Lord's blessing when settled on their mounts, turning useful livestock into acknowledgment of niʿma.
terra: The rider confesses the return to the Lord, redirecting the animal's benefit from possession toward its ultimate giver.
luna: This ayah places night and day, rain from heaven, and the revival of earth together; it connects the surah's night-day frame to the section's rain-grown field.

terra: Paradise contains rivers of milk whose taste does not change; this may offer a deliberately lasting milk-image against the source section's lexicographic milk that was expected to last but failed, though the ayah speaks of quality rather than supply.

luna: People are called to spend in God's way and some withhold; the ayah says the miser withholds from himself and contrasts human need with Allah's richness, matching the section's giver and miser. | terra: Those summoned to spend who act stingily are stingy only against themselves, the direct inverse of giving that purifies and benefits its giver.
terra: God completes His favor upon the Messenger and guides him on a straight path, another explicit convergence of favor brought to completion and guidance.

luna: The section's هدي is an animal meant to reach the sanctuary; here the offerings are held back from reaching it, making blocked passage the boundary to the completed rite. | terra: The hady is detained from reaching its place of sacrifice; this negative event makes the destination inherent in the source section's sense of هدي especially visible.
terra: A seedling puts out shoots, strengthens, thickens, and stands firm, offering a Quranic scene of gradual completion akin to the section's definition of Rabb's nurture stage by stage.

luna: Blessed rain produces gardens and harvested grain; the ayah gives a direct cloud-to-field instance of the section's growth image. | terra: Blessed rain grows gardens and harvest grain, giving the section's growth a literal source in descending blessing.

luna: Tall date palms with layered clusters grow from the watered land, recalling the section's palm yield and abundance. | terra: Tall date palms with layered clusters specify the fruit-bearing tree behind the source section's dictionary sense of itāʾ as a palm's yield.

luna: The rain and palm growth are provision for people, and the dead land is revived; crop growth becomes a sign of provision and return. | terra: The crop is provision for servants and rain revives dead land, completing the movement from blessing to growth and sustenance.

luna: The section contrasts a gift with repaying a favor; this ayah says a right for the asker and deprived is present in the believers' wealth, making giving a recognized claim rather than a personal debt. | terra: A recognized share of the giver's wealth belongs to the asker and deprived, corresponding to the crop's due that must be separated at harvest.
luna: The section's plant lexicon uses masculine and feminine categories; this ayah says created things come in pairs, a broader Quranic counterpart to differentiated growth.

luna: The section's root ز ك و names purification, while this ayah forbids people to claim purity and says Allah knows the God-fearing; it also says He knew them as embryos in their mothers' wombs. | terra: Humans are known even as embryos in their mothers' wombs and therefore must not declare themselves pure; womb, taqwa, and the boundary on self-purification meet in one ayah.

luna: The section uses the root س ع ي for the collector's work and for varied effort; this ayah says a person has only what he strives for, locating responsibility in each person's own action. | terra: A person has only what he strives for, supporting the section's contrast between an external collector and the giver who comes through his own saʿy.
terra: God creates the pair, male and female, repeating the created polarity from which the section extends its agricultural senses.
terra: That pair comes from an emitted drop, adding the reproductive origin behind the male/female formulation.

luna: The earth is laid out for creatures, beginning a passage that names fruit, date palms, grain, and fragrant plants; it gives the section's cultivated field a wider scene. | terra: The earth is laid out for living creatures, opening a provision scene of fruit, palms, and grain.

luna: Fruit and date palms with their sheaths are named as earth's yield, directly matching the section's palm and crop growth. | terra: Fruit and date palms with sheathed clusters name the yielding tree behind the source section's itāʾ imagery.
luna: Grain with husks and fragrant plants complete the yield; the ayah makes the earth's provision concrete in crops. | terra: Husked grain and fragrant plants complete the earth's crop provision.
terra: The refrain asks which favors of the Lord can be denied immediately after the crop inventory, joining niʿma, Rabb, and kadhaba around agricultural provision.
terra: Everything on earth passes away, the necessary first half of the boundary completed by the enduring face of the Lord in 55:27.
terra: The face of the Lord possessed of majesty and honor remains after all earthly things pass, identifying the enduring object sought by the giver.

luna: The ayah asks what people sow, introducing a direct crop image behind the section's growth language. | terra: The question أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ fixes attention on the human act of sowing that precedes, but does not cause, growth.

luna: It asks whether people make the crop grow or God does; this makes explicit that the section's growth of field, palm, and giver comes from divine nurture. | terra: The next question asks whether people cause the seed to grow or God does, sharply assigning the section's growth to the true nurturer.
luna: God could make the crop dry debris after it grows; this gives the field's increase a specific limit and reversal.
terra: The reader is made to consider the water people drink, shifting attention from possessed provision to its source.
terra: The question asks whether humans send water down from the rain cloud or God does, a direct correction to independent claims over the source of growth.
terra: God could make that water bitter, setting a boundary on the apparently secure provision that feeds fields and herds.
terra: After the surrounding signs of crops and water, people make their response to provision an act of denial, joining rizq to kadhaba in the negative way the section dramatizes.

luna: Like the section's giver whose outlay grows rather than diminishes, the one who gives Allah a good loan is promised multiplication and noble reward. | terra: The one who lends God a good loan receives it multiplied and a noble reward, aligning increase with a Godward gift rather than a human repayment.
luna: God revives the earth after its death; this broadens the section's field-growth image into a direct statement about the giver of life.
terra: Male and female almsgivers who lend God a good loan have it multiplied, expressing charitable giving as increase rather than depletion.

luna: The section links field growth to wealth; this ayah compares worldly life to rain-fed plants that flourish, yellow, and become debris, while people boast in wealth and children, making the crop's growth temporary. | terra: Vegetation pleasing its cultivators later withers, yellows, and becomes debris, a boundary against mistaking visible growth of wealth for lasting increase.
terra: Those who are stingy and command stinginess are warned that God is self-sufficient, the theological inverse of imagining that retained wealth enriches its owner or that God needs the gift.
luna: The section distinguishes personal giving from a collector's assessment; this ayah makes charity before private consultation an act that is better and purer for the giver.

luna: This ayah directs distributed wealth to the Messenger, relatives, orphans, needy, and traveler so it will not circulate only among the rich; it extends the section's alms collection into social distribution.

luna: The section contrasts the giver with the one who withholds; this ayah praises people who give others preference even when they themselves are in need. | terra: Those who prefer others despite their own need and are guarded from selfish greed enact the non-reciprocal generosity of the section's giver.
terra: A messenger among the unlettered recites, purifies, and teaches them, repeating communal purification through revelation rather than wealth.

luna: This ayah warns believers not to let wealth and children divert them from remembering Allah; it identifies one way property defeats its owner, while 63:10 adds the urgency to spend before death. | terra: Wealth and children must not distract believers from remembering God; it introduces the command in 63:10 to spend before death closes the opportunity.

luna: The section says wealth will not avail when a person falls; this ayah urges spending from God's provision before death arrives, when the latecomer wishes for more time to give charity. | terra: The dying person asks for delay in order to give charity and become righteous, showing that wealth must be released voluntarily before its opportunity ends.
terra: Wealth and children are a test immediately before the command to spend, framing property as the arena in which generosity or withholding is disclosed.

luna: The section's donor overcomes withholding; this ayah says those protected from the soul's stinginess are successful, naming the inner boundary that giving crosses. | terra: The command to spend is said to be good for one's own souls, directly matching the section's claim that the giver's purification returns to himself.
terra: A good loan to God is multiplied and forgiven, joining charitable expenditure, increase, and cleansing.
terra: Whoever fears God has his affair made easy, tightly joining taqwa to divine yusr as 92:5-7 does.
terra: The wealthy and constrained are each commanded to spend from what God gave, and the ayah promises ease after hardship; spending and the y-s-r branch meet in an economic setting.

luna: This parable begins with garden owners who intend to harvest its fruit, matching the section's crop and harvest image before revealing the consequence of withholding. | terra: The owners of a garden are tested after resolving to harvest it at dawn, opening a sustained reversal of the section's crop-giver scene.
terra: They make their harvest oath without qualification, exposing the self-sufficient stance later corrected by the Lord's destruction of the crop.

luna: While the garden owners sleep, a visitation passes over their garden; the sudden loss reverses the crop's expected growth and harvest. | terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while its owners sleep, assigning the failure of expected yield to the power beyond the cultivators.

luna: The orchard is left like a harvested field, contrasting a hoped-for yield with a crop destroyed before its owners share it. | terra: The garden becomes like a dark, stripped field, the visual opposite of the crop that increases and gives fruit.
terra: The owners call one another early, beginning the deliberate attempt to secure the harvest for themselves.
terra: They hurry to harvest if they are going to cut the crop, fixing the episode at the same moment when 6:141 commands that the crop's right be given.
terra: They set out whispering together, showing that exclusion from the harvest is planned rather than accidental.

luna: The owners whisper that no poor person should enter the garden, directly reversing the section's giver who lets wealth flow outward. | terra: Their stated purpose is that no poor person enter the garden that day, a direct reversal of giving the crop's due at harvest.

luna: They go out intent on keeping the harvest to themselves, making withholding the purpose of their crop journey. | terra: They go out convinced of their power to withhold, opposing the giver who recognizes yield as the Lord's provision.

luna: When they see the garden destroyed, they recognize they have lost the crop; this makes the section's harvest due a pointed contrast to selfish possession. | terra: On seeing the ruined garden they first think they have lost the way, registering how completely expected abundance has vanished.

luna: The owners admit they have been deprived after denying the poor a share; the ayah joins withheld provision to its loss. | terra: They realize that they have been deprived, the crop analogue of the source section's milk expected to continue but suddenly cut off.

luna: One among them asks whether they had glorified God, locating the failure in their refusal to recognize the source of the garden's provision. | terra: The most balanced owner asks why they did not glorify God, restoring the Lordward stance absent from their harvest plan.

luna: The garden owners acknowledge their wrongdoing; their confession contrasts with the section's giver who acts in piety from the outset. | terra: They finally glorify their Lord and confess wrongdoing, belatedly acknowledging the true nurturer of the garden.
terra: They name themselves transgressors after intending to deny the poor, exposing the moral failure behind the barren field.
terra: They hope their Lord will replace the garden with something better and turn their desire toward Him, reversing self-reliant possession after the crop's loss.
luna: The garden's destruction is called punishment, and a greater punishment remains; it reinforces the limit of crop and property when used selfishly.
terra: The condemned person says his wealth did not avail him, an almost exact first-person enactment of 92:11.

luna: The section's crop has a due on harvest; this ayah describes a known share in believers' wealth, a parallel form of a designated right. | terra: The worshippers' wealth contains a known right, making charitable transfer a due within wealth rather than repayment of a private favor.
terra: That known right is for the asker and the deprived, identifying the human destination of the wealth that is given for God.
luna: Noah's call to seek forgiveness is followed by rain from heaven, joining purification to the source of growth.
luna: The rain is promised in abundance, directly matching the section's cloud that grows vegetation.
luna: Wealth, children, gardens, and rivers are promised together; this ayah gathers the section's material and agricultural signs in a single promise.
terra: God has created human beings in stages, a concise parallel to the section's definition of tarbiya as bringing something through successive states.
terra: God is said to have grown human beings from the earth as a growth, supporting the section's passage from plant development to human moral increase.
terra: The ayah joins giving zakat, lending God a good loan, and finding with God whatever good one advances, gathering charity, divine receipt, and return.

luna: The section's giver does not pay back a favor; this command not to give while seeking a greater return marks the boundary between a gift and a transaction. | terra: The command not to confer a favor seeking increase plausibly marks the same boundary as 92:19-20: a gift is not a claim on a larger human return.
terra: The condemned person neither confirms the truth nor prays, restaging the failed ṣ-d-q stance of 92:9 and 92:16.
terra: Instead he denies and turns away, reproducing in one ayah the paired actions كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ of 92:16.
terra: The human begins as an emitted drop, opening another staged account of sexed creation.
terra: The drop becomes a clot and is created and proportioned, contributing the gradual formation associated with the section's nurture language.

luna: The source section's roots ذ ك ر and ء ن ث are used in its agricultural glosses; this ayah uses الذكر والأنثى for the two sexes created from a drop, a human reproductive sense of the same pair. | terra: God makes from it the two sexes, male and female, explicitly repeating 92:3.

luna: The giver in the section parts with wealth freely; this ayah depicts people giving food to the needy, orphan, and captive despite loving it, showing generosity as a concrete release of what one values. | terra: Food is given despite love for it to the needy, orphan, and captive; 76:9 then states that this materially costly gift seeks only God's face.

luna: The section says the giver seeks the Face of his Lord without repaying a human favor; this ayah states that food is given for Allah's face without seeking reward or thanks from people. | terra: The feeders say they give only for God's face and want neither recompense nor thanks; this is the clearest parallel to giving without a human favor that must be repaid.
terra: Abundant water poured from rain clouds starts a concise sequence of grain, plants, and gardens.
terra: The rain brings forth grain and vegetation, the crop increase at the center of the section's zakat image.
terra: Dense gardens complete the rain-grown sequence as a scene of abundant yield.
terra: God brings the earth's water and pasture out of it, presenting the provision that sustains the herd.
terra: Water and pasture are explicitly enjoyment for people and their livestock, matching the two beneficiaries joined throughout the section.

luna: Rain is poured down from above, the opening action in a sequence that moves from watered ground to grain, fruit, and pasture. | terra: Poured water begins a sequence that ends as provision for people and livestock, so this ayah supplies the rain-source of the joined field-and-herd scene.

luna: The ground is split open for growth, a direct agricultural counterpart to the section's fertile soil. | terra: The earth is split open before growth, making the prepared ground in the section's fertile-soil imagery concrete.

luna: Grain is brought forth from the split earth, the crop growth that the section also hears within zakat's root. | terra: Grain is grown from the split earth, the basic crop whose increase supports the section's zakat metaphor.

luna: Grapes and fodder follow the grain, showing the field feeding people and animals. | terra: Grapes and fresh fodder appear together, bringing human crop and animal feed into the same agricultural sequence.
luna: Olives and date palms follow, matching the section's dictionary image of the palm's yield. | terra: Olives and date palms name the tree whose abundant yield the section uses to explain itāʾ.
luna: Dense gardens appear in the sequence, extending the field into cultivated abundance. | terra: Dense gardens broaden the productive landscape that rain brings forth.
luna: Fruit and pasture are provided, linking human harvest and animal feed in one ayah. | terra: Fruit and pasture place orchard yield beside the forage needed by the herd.

luna: The entire preceding yield is provision for people and their livestock, making the crop-and-herd meeting explicit. | terra: The entire sequence of water, split earth, grain, palms, and pasture is finally named provision for people and their livestock, stating the meeting that the section develops.
terra: No soul possesses anything for another on that day and command belongs to God, the ultimate boundary around human repayment and substitution.
terra: The command to glorify the name of رَبِّكَ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ gives the exact divine title sought in 92:20 and supplies the giver's Lordward stance.
terra: The Most High is the one who creates and proportions, connecting 87:1's Rabb to the created male and female and to the section's idea of making a thing fit.
terra: The same Lord determines and guides, bringing measure and hidaya together immediately before the pasture image.
terra: God brings out the pasture, directly staging the vegetation that feeds the section's herd under the care of Rabb al-Aʿlā.
terra: The pasture is made dark stubble after being brought forth, a precise vegetal counterpart to increase that unexpectedly ceases.

luna: The section reads 92:7's root ي س ر through a lexicon's image of a flock's abundant yield; this matching promise, We shall ease you toward ease, preserves the Quranic ease sense alongside that concrete gloss. | terra: وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ closely repeats the promise-form and destination of 92:7, while the same surah later names the one who purifies himself.
luna: The command to remind whoever benefits from reminder matches the surah's warning that precedes the giver's purification and the contrast with the denier.
luna: This ayah says the one who fears will take the reminder, matching the section's giver among the God-fearing and the surah's promised ease.
luna: The next ayah says the most wretched will avoid the reminder, completing 87:10's division between the one who fears and the one who turns away as in the section's two paths.

luna: The section connects ز ك و with giving and growth; this ayah announces that the one who purifies himself succeeds, with purification as the visible result. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ makes self-purification the condition of flourishing, the outcome enacted by the giver of 92:18.
terra: After the successful person purifies himself in 87:14, he remembers his Lord's name and prays; this gives that purification its Godward orientation, as 92:20 does.

luna: The section pairs a giver with one who withholds; this rebuke says people fail to honor the orphan, then continues with their neglect of feeding the poor. | terra: Failure to honor the orphan begins a sequence opposing the section's purifying use of wealth.

luna: The section's gift releases provision to others; this ayah names the failure to urge feeding the poor as a sign of moral neglect. | terra: They do not encourage feeding the poor, reversing the sacrificial and agricultural gift directed to the needy.

luna: The section's giver parts with wealth; this ayah condemns consuming inheritance greedily, the opposite use of property. | terra: They consume inheritance greedily, turning received property inward instead of recognizing a due within it.

luna: This ayah names intense love of wealth in the same rebuke of neglecting orphans and the poor; it sharpens the section's contrast between giving and withholding. | terra: Their excessive love of wealth names the attachment overcome by the person who gives his māl to purify himself.
luna: The section's surah ends by saying the giver will be satisfied; this ayah addresses the tranquil soul returning to its Lord, carrying the same stance into the closing scene.
luna: The soul is described as satisfied and pleasing to God, a close counterpart to the section's promise that the giver will be content.
luna: The satisfied soul is invited among God's servants; 89:28 contributes its approval, and this row contributes belonging to the company of the accepted.
luna: The next invitation is to enter God's garden, completing 89:27-29's return and approval with the promised destination.
luna: The section's giving is a chosen costly act; this ayah asks what the steep path is, then answers with freeing a person and feeding the hungry.
luna: Freeing a slave is the first concrete deed in the steep path, showing release of another person as one form of giving beyond the section's wealth.
luna: The steep path continues with feeding in a day of hunger, paralleling the provision released by the section's generous giver.
luna: This ayah specifies an orphan near of kin among those fed on the hard day, sharpening the recipients of the section's generosity.
luna: The next recipient is a poor person in severe need; it gives the feeding image a precise human counterpart to the section's charitable wealth.

luna: The source section's root ز ك و evokes growth; this ayah says success belongs to the one who purifies the soul, in direct contrast to the following ayah's corruption of it. | terra: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا locates success in purifying the soul and supplies the immediately preceding surah's transitive counterpart to يَتَزَكَّىٰ.
terra: The one who buries or corrupts the soul fails, furnishing the immediate opposite to the purifier who flourishes in 91:9.
terra: The command to speak of one's Lord's blessing locates niʿma with Rabb, whereas 92:19 denies that the giver acts to repay a human niʿma.
luna: The ayah says the human being transgresses, setting up the section's description of one who becomes self-sufficient and withholds.
luna: The specific cause is that a person sees himself as self-sufficient; this directly parallels the source surah's root غ ن ي in its description of the miser's imagined independence.
luna: The ayah says the return is to the Lord, a boundary on imagined self-sufficiency that completes the section's contrast between worldly wealth and the giver seeking his Lord's face.
terra: The person who gathers and repeatedly counts wealth is the concentrated opposite of one who releases wealth for purification.
terra: He imagines his wealth will make him last, an explicit false confidence in māl like the expectation that yield will never cease.

luna: The section compares denial of the good to milk drying unexpectedly; this ayah's denier of the judgment is the person whose conduct toward vulnerable people is then exposed. | terra: Denial of judgment is introduced as the source of a social failure, linking kadhaba to the opposite of truthful giving rather than to words alone.

luna: The section opposes its giver to withholding; the next description of the denier is one who repels the orphan, a concrete refusal of care. | terra: The denier drives away the orphan, enacting the hard refusal opposed to the section's voluntary giver.

luna: This ayah condemns failing to urge feeding the poor, a direct social opposite to the section's gift of wealth and the food given in 76:8. | terra: He does not urge feeding the poor, the human consequence of denial set against charity and harvest rights.
terra: The command فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ directs sacrifice specifically to the Lord, matching the section's animal gift whose true orientation is the face of its Rabb.
terra: Abu Lahab's wealth and acquisitions do not avail him, another direct reversal of confidence in accumulated māl.
